problem: The comparison sign is missing: the text reads "λ  1 is lean (excess air)", so the sentence states nothing, and a student can read it as λ less than 1 being lean, which is the opposite of the truth.
fix: Write it out in words to avoid the stripped symbol: "λ greater than 1 is lean (excess air); λ less than 1 is rich (excess fuel)."

problem: Same missing sign: "The narrowband output is about 0.9 V at λ  1." The high-voltage case is rich, i.e. λ less than 1, so as printed the bullet contradicts itself (high voltage stated for the lean side).
fix: "The narrowband output is about 0.9 V on the rich side, at λ less than 1 (for example λ = 0.9)."

problem: "roughly 0.7 to air" is unclear. Air is not a λ value on the same scale; the upper end is free air, λ tending to infinity.
fix: "roughly from λ = 0.7 up to free air (λ tending to infinity)."
